transcript: You should see these New York theatre productions before they close in July. Closing the soonest is And Then the Rodeo Burned Down by Xhloe and Natasha, the clown duo that's very much on the rise right now. And this is a Rodeo themed show with a metatheatrical twist. And we have the musical adaptation of Girl Interrupted, which is definitely not for everybody. It's a very unconventional musical with some very dark subject matter, but I thought it was gorgeous. Then we have Camping, which takes place in the same tent over many years, and it's about a pair of best friends who may or may not be something more. Dad, Don’t Read This is a very buzzy new play about a group of girls at a series of sleepovers. One of them in particular is going through a pretty rough time and uses the Sims as an escape. The Broadway revival of proof, starring Ayo Edebiri and Don Cheadle, is closing soon. I will say I didn't love this show, but I did love both of their performances, and I was glad I saw it for that reason. We have the National Asian American Theatre Company's production of Henry VI, told in two parts. I didn't see this run, but I saw it when they did it in 2018, and I loved it. For me, it was a definitive version of the Henry VI plays. Big Feelings is like an immersive, interactive play taking place in a first Grade classroom, where you are one of the students. And I found this one extremely delightful, although it goes to some very dark places. I haven't seen Birthright yet, but I've been hearing exquisite things about it. This is the same playwright as Eureka Day, and I believe it's about a group of friends who reunite after a birthright trip. And if you don't know what birthright is, google it. We have the Jennifer Nettles musical Giulia, which is a true story about a 17th century female apothecary. I'm also looking forward to this new musical of the Potluck by Cesar Alvarez, who is a really exciting indie musical theatre artist. And I believe they actually have a personal connection to the historical events in the show. The Broadway revival of August Wilson's Joe Turner's Come and gone is closing. This is a really exquisite play, and I don't think you should miss the opportunity to see it performed at this high of a level. Finally, the Classical Theatre of Harlem production of Othello. This is one of the other free outdoor Shakespeare things that happens annually, and it's just as good, if not sometimes better, than the Public's.
classificationReason: Roundup of 6+ NYC shows closing in July (And Then the Rodeo Burned Down, Girl Interrupted, Camping, Dad Don't Read This, Proof, Henry VI), with no single show as the primary focus.
